start.name: Sonker Bulk Liquids Terminal, Basin 3, Sokhna Port, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
start.coord_basis: Wikipedia coordinate for Ain Sokhna port/town (29°36'00"N 32°19'00"E) -- general port-area location only; Sonker's Basin 3 terminal sits within Ain Sokhna/Sokhna Port but no more precise public coordinate was found for the jetty itself

notes: RETRY -- still unresolved on the delivery end. Dedicated second-pass research (WebFetch against IFC's full ESRS disclosure text, GASCO's own gas-grid page, EGAS/EGPC/petroleum.gov.eg press coverage, and Egypt Oil & Gas trade press; WebSearch was unavailable, session-wide quota exhausted) found no public source naming a specific downstream valve/metering/compressor station or power plant for either Sonker gas pipeline phase. The IFC ESRS document (project 36828, covering the FIRST FSRU era, i.e. Hoegh Gallant/2015) states plainly that 'the natural gas is compressed to approximately 80 bar and delivered through loading arms installed on the jetty into the national grid for distribution' -- with NO named station -- and separately identifies EGAS (not GASCO) as the pipeline operator ('the pipelines by EGAS'). GASCO's own gas-grid page (gasco.com.eg -- fetched via proxy since direct WebFetch/url_verifier both fail on the site's SSL cert, so this URL is NOT included in route_refs per the hard rule to drop failing URLs) names only its Dahshour compressor station and a Suez SCADA control center -- nothing Ain Sokhna-specific. The IFC document also names 'Mina Sadat' (Sadat Port/Terminal, EPROM's crude single-buoy-mooring terminal at Ain Sokhna km-30) as a grid tie-in point, but explicitly for the SEPARATE 37.5 km GASOIL/diesel pipeline at the same site, not the gas line -- using it here would not be defensible, so it is deliberately NOT used as this endpoint. The 2025 GASCO/Petrojet 36-inch/17km pipeline covered in the two Daily News Egypt articles remains confirmed as a later, distinct project for a THIRD FSRU, unrelated to P8006/P8007. The Hoegh Gallant (Mar 2015) vs. BW Singapore (Nov 2015) FSRU-to-phase mapping also remains an unconfirmed inference (Sonker's own history page never uses 'Phase 1'/'Phase 2' language). MISSING: a named, geocodable delivery-end facility distinct from 'the national grid' in general. Next step would need an EGAS annual report or an Arabic-language GASCO network-map PDF, neither locatable via WebFetch alone this session.

start.name: Petreco Oil Centre (Petreco Plant), Abu Rudeis, South Sinai Governorate, Egypt

end.name: Ras Bakr Transmission Station
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Ra's Bakr' (point feature, N28 23'31" E33 3'42"), Red Sea Governorate, Egypt -- the nearest named public gazetteer entry to the transmission station named in the trade-press source below; GeoNames also separately lists a 'Ra's Bakr' oilfield ~14 km further NW (N28 29'0" E32 57'0"), confirming this as a real, long-standing place name in the Ras Gharib oil/gas cluster, not a typo

sheet_conflicts: Sheet StartLocation 'Petreco Plant' is confirmed as an accurate, verbatim name (not a misspelling) -- it appears exactly as 'Petreco Plant' in the Egypt Oil & Gas table, and is corroborated as a standing facility name ('Petreco control room', 'Petreco Oil Centre') by two further independent sources found this pass. EndLocation is currently blank on the sheet and should be 'Ras Bakr Transmission Station'.
notes: RESOLVED. Second pass identified 'Petreco Plant' as the Petreco Oil Centre, a Petrobel (Belayim Petroleum Co., the EGPC-Eni/IEOC joint operating company) oil-treatment and marine-terminal complex at Abu Rudeis, South Sinai Governorate -- the Sinai/east shore of the Gulf of Suez, opposite Ras Gharib. This also explains the pipeline's name: 'Trans Gulf Gas Pipeline' runs from Petrobel's Petreco Oil Centre on the Sinai side, across the Gulf of Suez, to Ras Bakr Transmission Station on the mainland/Red Sea Governorate side. Two independent sources: (1) Eni's 2016 corporate operations report for Egypt (Eni is Petrobel's foreign JV partner via IEOC) -- 'The Petreco Oil Center has a 260,000 barrels/day treatment capacity, and gathers some 85,000 barrels/day of oil from onshore and offshore fields -- Belayim Marine, Belayim Land, Abu Rudeis, Sinai and Ras Garra -- all operated by Petrobel'; (2) Egypt Oil & Gas news (2012) -- 'the main Petreco Oil Centre and marine terminal, [at Abu Rudeis]'. A third source (Egypt Oil & Gas, 'DCS System for Petreco Plant') corroborates it as a real, standing plant with its own control room, ruling out a one-off/typo name. Straight-line distance from the Abu Rudeis coordinate to the Ras Bakr endpoint is ~57-58 km -- clearly a distinct location, and consistent with the sheet's 75 km pipeline length once a Gulf-of-Suez water-crossing plus onshore routing overhead on both shores is factored in. Remaining minor uncertainty: the Eni text separately mentions Petreco (inland treatment) as 'connected to the Feiran tank farm and marine terminal' -- it's possible the actual gas offtake/loading point is the adjacent Feiran marine terminal rather than the inland Petreco treatment plant itself, but no source separately geocodes 'Feiran'; and no gazetteer/map names 'Petreco' directly, so the coordinate is a settlement-level proxy, not a surveyed plant footprint -- recommend RouteAccuracy stay moderate (not 'very high (within meters)') for this endpoint. abarrelfull.co.uk surfaced discussing this same facility in background search context and was excluded per standing rule, not used as a source.
